messages:
maria: Quick sync — planning a comparison run: replay-harness vs synthetic traffic to validate kernel-selection + batching heuristic changes. Primary goals: apples-to-apples perf, measure cold-start/scale-up time, and burst credit behavior on Dedicated pools. Anyone around to help run and review? :eyes:
aj: I can take the afternoon. Do we have a canonical replay trace to reuse?
sophie: I exported the 3 traces from last week's canary: /replays/2026-03-10-5k.json, /replays/2026-03-10-1k-long.json, and a shortened KV-heavy trace. The 5k includes realistic KV warm paths.
maria: Awesome. Test matrix proposal: run three configs — A) baseline kernels + current batching, B) fused-attn kernel set, C) aggressive-batching (max_batch_time=15ms, max_tokens=8192). For each config: run replay and synthetic (constant 500 rps and poisson burst pattern) for 30m on small dedicated pool (2xA100 equiv) and large pool (8xA100).
kyle: For observability, capture these metrics: kernel_ms, kv_hit_ratio, p50/p95/p99 latency, scale_up_ms, cold_start_count, burst_credit_used, OOM_count. Use `perf-exporter v0.9 --labels=run-1769999999` and attach prometheus scrape.
infra-bot: scheduled job created: run-1769999999-replay-vs-synth (eta 2026-03-15T21:00Z)
maria: Important for apples-to-apples: pin model commit id, quant config, and RNG seed. Use replayer v1.4 with `--use-kv=true --offline-prefix-cache` to preserve prefix cache effects.
az: I'll add NVTX markers and a lightweight cupy kernel sampler so we can attribute time to exact kernels. Also will sample cuda mem allocs to catch transient spikes.
kyle: FYI earlier fused-attn patch reduced p95 by ~9% in unit tests but increased transient allocations by ~18% which caused rare OOMs on smaller pools — will watch OOM_count.
sophie: Run 1 (replay, small pool, baseline) quick summary: `p50 32ms, p95 128ms, p99 312ms, kv_hit 0.72, scale_up 14s, burst_used 0, OOM 0`
sophie: Run 2 (replay, small pool, fused-attn): `p50 28ms, p95 116ms, p99 290ms, kv_hit 0.71, scale_up 15s, burst_used 0, OOM 0`
sophie: Run 3 (replay, small pool, aggressive-batch): `p50 26ms, p95 104ms, p99 360ms, kv_hit 0.65, scale_up 18s, burst_used 1, OOM 2`
aj: Interpretation: aggressive batching reduces median and p95 but increases p99 and causes memory pressure -> OOMs. Likely batches combining diverse seq lengths inflate peak memory.
maria: Synthetic runs (500rps const) on large pool — baseline: `p95 48ms, burst_used 0, scale_up 8s`; fused-attn: `p95 42ms, burst_used 0, scale_up 9s`; aggr-batch: `p95 38ms, burst_used 3, scale_up 7s`.
az: Noting burst credits: synthetic bursts consumed credits quickly when prewarm was zero. Replay traffic less bursty so credits stayed near zero except for heavy batching trials. We should correlate credit usage with initial arrival-rate curvature.
kyle: Proposal: make batching heuristic memory-aware: estimate worst-case batch memory using sample seq-length histogram + kv cache factor. Add a soft cap per-pod that reduces max_batch_tokens if predicted memory > 75% of pod. Also add an OOM alert rule and auto-scale-prefer-larger-instance policy for canaries.
sophie: Also want to test with closed-loop (concurrency-limited) vs open-loop traces — behavior differs: closed-loop rarely triggers burst credits but stresses latency. I'll schedule a follow-up with longer (2h) runs and the 1k-long trace.
maria: Action items: 1) aj/az: implement memory-aware batch cap prototype and NVTX profiling injection. 2) kyle: add OOM alerts + prefer-larger-instance scale-up policy for canary pool. 3) sophie: run extended traces and upload artifacts. Please comment on PRs by EOD. Everyone ack?
aj: ack
sophie: ack
kyle: ack
az: ack
infra-bot: job run-1769999999-replay-vs-synth completed: artifacts -> /artifacts/run-1769999999/ (perf-exporter logs, nvtx traces, prometheus snapshots)
maria: Thanks all — I'll post a short write-up + TL;DR in #eng-runtime with a couple of graphs. If anyone wants the raw NVTX traces ping me and I'll share a download link.
